_doc: Open-ended test/exam questions graded by AI (server) against the rubric. subject = curriculum code; levels = [min, max] year (1=JSS1..6=SS3). keyPoints also drive the offline fallback grader.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short informal letter (3-5 sentences) to a friend telling them about your first week in boarding school.
questions.rubric: Informal letter format and friendly tone; describes the first week; correct sentences.
keyPoints: Uses an informal greeting such as 'Dear' and the friend's name
Mentions events or feelings from the first week
Closes with a sign-off such as 'Your friend'

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Explain what 'concord' (subject-verb agreement) means and give one correct and one incorrect example sentence.
questions.rubric: Correct definition, a correct example and an incorrect example identified.
keyPoints: Concord means the verb agrees with its subject in number
A singular subject takes a singular verb
Gives an incorrect example and says why it is wrong

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: In a short paragraph, argue whether phones should be allowed in boarding schools.
questions.rubric: Clear position, at least two reasons, an example, and a conclusion; coherent paragraph.
keyPoints: States a clear position (for or against)
Supports a reason with an example

questions.subject: LIT
questions.q: In Things Fall Apart, what causes Okonkwo's downfall? Give two reasons.
questions.rubric: Identifies personal flaws and external forces with reference to the novel.
keyPoints: His fear of weakness / being like his father Unoka
His exile after accidentally killing a clansman
The arrival of the missionaries and colonial government changing Umuofia
Refers to specific events in the novel

questions.subject: LIT
questions.q: What is the difference between a simile and a metaphor? Give one example of each.
questions.rubric: Correct definitions and an example of each.
keyPoints: A metaphor compares directly without 'like' or 'as'

questions.subject: GOV
questions.q: Name the three arms of government and explain the function of each.
questions.rubric: All three arms named with a correct function for each.
keyPoints: The judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes
Mentions separation of powers or checks and balances
Nigerian example such as the National Assembly, the President or the Supreme Court

questions.subject: GOV
questions.q: State and explain three features of democracy.
questions.rubric: Three correct features, each briefly explained.
keyPoints: Freedom of speech and the press
Majority rule with respect for minority rights

questions.subject: CIV
questions.q: What are national values? Mention three national values and why they matter.
questions.rubric: Definition plus three values with a reason.
keyPoints: National values are beliefs and standards a country expects its citizens to uphold
Explains why they help the country develop or live in peace

questions.subject: CIV
questions.q: List two rights and two duties of a Nigerian citizen.
questions.rubric: Two correct rights and two correct duties.
keyPoints: Right to education / freedom of expression / freedom of movement / religion
Duty to obey the laws of the land
Duty to pay taxes / vote / respect the flag and anthem / defend the nation

questions.subject: SOS
questions.q: Explain two types of family and two functions of the family.
questions.rubric: Two types with brief explanation, two functions.
keyPoints: Nuclear family: father, mother and children
Extended family: includes grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins

questions.subject: RS
questions.q: Why is honesty important? Support your answer with a lesson from your religion and an example from school life.
questions.rubric: Explains why honesty matters, a religious reference and a school example.
keyPoints: A religious teaching or story about honesty
An example from school life such as not cheating in exams

questions.subject: ECO
questions.q: State the law of demand and give two factors other than price that affect demand.
questions.rubric: Correct law of demand, and two non-price factors.
keyPoints: The higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded (other things being equal)
